newsitem.title: USA: Next Fed move likely rate hike --Ex Fed Gov Angell.
newsitem.headline: Next Fed move likely rate hike --Ex Fed Gov Angell.

text.p: Former Federal Reserve Governor Wayne Angell said Thursday the U.S. central bank is more likely to raise than lower interest rates, but he does not see any action coming over the short term.

"I believe that even with gold below $370 an ounce...the next move of the Federal Reserve is more likely to be higher rather than lower," said Angell, chief economist at Bear, Stearns and Co Inc speaking to investors at the firm.
"But, I do not see such a move coming over the short-run forecast horizon," he added.
Angell said the recent strength of the dollar against European currencies and gold hints that U.S. monetary policy has become less stimulative.
"Looking at the U.S. economy today,...recent developments indicate that monetary policy is somewhat less accommodative than it appeared six months ago," Angell said.
"The dollar appears to be somewhat stronger against gold, the Deutschemark, and I guess even against the Mexican peso," he added.

Regarding the outlook on wage pressures in the U.S., Angell predicted average hourly earnings would rise 0.3 percent per annum over the next few years. He did not view this expected rise as inflationary.
"I believe that average hourly earnings in the United States are going to continue to rise," Angell said.

"Every year, average hourly earnings in the United States are going to be three-tenths of one percent higher. That is, this time next year average hourly earnings will be advancing at a 3.7 percent rate," he said.
